Then \(S_1=\mathrm{Im}\,P\) has dimension \(d-m\) against \(d(M)=d-1\): deficit \(m-1>0\), an apex as for VeRA.

coord_notes.covariance: Covariance holds only in law, but the structured part is deterministic: in \(P=HG\Pi HB\) the random \(B,\Pi,G\) randomise the inner side, while the outer Walsh-Hadamard \(H\) acts on \(\Theta\). The law of \(\mathrm{Im}\,P\) is invariant exactly under \(H\,B_D\,H^{-1}\) (\(B_D\) the signed permutations), which contains a coordinate or neuron permutation of \(\Theta\) only when it is a Hadamard automorphism (a dyadic shift). So the flattening order and the dyadic Hadamard structure are imposed (\(\Pi\)), unlike the dense Gaussian projection Fastfood emulates (which would be \(O(D)\)-covariant in law, 'frame'). The frame is also shared by all boxes, so Obs II.15's per-box hypothesis fails.
coord_notes.rebasing: With \(P\) frozen, \(R_\infty=\theta_0+\mathrm{span}\,C=\theta_0+\bigoplus_j\mathrm{Im}\,P_j\) (per-layer row blocks of \(P\)), strictly larger than DID's single subspace: the SAID analogue of \(\mathrm{VeRA}^\infty=\) LoRA-FA.

coord_notes.shape: \(\Delta W=\alpha\,\mathcal H^{-1}(\Delta H)\) is linear in the n trained coefficients: a coordinate subspace in the real 2-D Hartley frame.
coord_notes.base_point: The exactly pointed variant (zero coefficients) is regular. The paper's Kaiming init of the coefficients leaves a defect \(\alpha\mathcal H^{-1}(\Delta H_0)\), treated like FourierFT's '≈' in the table.
coord_notes.gauge: The Hartley basis \(\mathrm{cas}=\cos+\sin\) is real and orthogonal with no conjugate-pair identification, so \(\rho\) is injective (unlike FourierFT, which gains +1 per sampled conjugate pair).
coord_notes.covariance: The DHT imposes cyclic index structure on rows and columns (\(\Pi\)).
